🧮 Part 3 - Typed Arrays and Tuples in TypeScript - The Ultimate Guide
📦 Why Arrays and Tuples Matter
Arrays are one of the most common data structures - but in JavaScript, they can quickly become chaotic:
let items = [1, "two", true]; items.push({}); // 😬 No error in JS!
TypeScript brings order by enforcing what kind of data an array can hold - and with tuples, you can even control the exact structure of an array.
Let’s break it down.
🧱 Typed Arrays
You can type arrays in two ways, both equivalent:
let scores: number[] = [85, 90, 95]; let names: Array = ["Alice", "Bob", "Charlie"];
✅ Both forms tell TypeScript:
“This array will contain only numbers” or “only strings.”
If you try to push something else:
scores.push("Ninety"); // ❌ Error: Argument of type 'string' is not assignable to parameter of type 'number'
💡 TypeScript Infers Types Automatically
let fruits = ["apple", "banana", "cherry"]; fruits.push("orange"); // ✅ OK fruits.push(5); // ❌ Error: number not assignable to string
Even without annotations, TS knows fruits is string[].
🔒 Readonly Arrays
Sometimes you want to protect arrays from modification. That’s where readonly arrays come in.
let numbers: readonly number[] = [1, 2, 3]; numbers.push(4); // ❌ Error: Property 'push' does not exist on type 'readonly number[]'
You can read from them, but not mutate them.
console.log(numbers[0]); // ✅ Allowed numbers[0] = 10; // ❌ Error
Perfect for:
•
Immutable constants
•
API response data
•
Functional programming patterns
🧠 ReadonlyArray` Generic Form
The long form is:
let colors: ReadonlyArray = ["red", "green", "blue"];
Equivalent to:
let colors: readonly string[] = ["red", "green", "blue"];
Both prevent modification methods like .push(), .pop(), .splice().
🧩 Tuples - Fixed Structure Arrays
Tuples are arrays with a specific number of elements, each with a defined type and position.
let user: [string, number] = ["Pavan", 25];
✅ The first element must be a string ✅ The second must be a number
user = ["Ravi", 30]; // ✅ OK user = [30, "Ravi"]; // ❌ Error
💡 Tuple Destructuring
You can unpack tuples just like arrays:
let [name, age] = user; console.log(`${name} is ${age} years old.`);
This gives a cleaner, readable way to extract values.
⚙️ Optional and Rest Elements in Tuples
TypeScript 4+ supports optional and rest elements inside tuples - super useful for flexible data.
Optional Elements
let userInfo: [string, number?]; userInfo = ["Pavan"]; userInfo = ["Pavan", 28];
Here, the second value (number) is optional.
Rest Elements
Tuples can have variable-length ends:
let rgb: [number, ...string[]]; rgb = [255, "red", "green", "blue"];
Useful when you know the first few types, but not the rest (e.g., command args, coordinates, dynamic lists).
🧠 Tuples vs Arrays - Quick Comparison
| Feature | Array | Tuple | | ---------------- | ----------------------- | ----------------------------------- | | Type consistency | Same type for all items | Different types allowed | | Length | Variable | Fixed or predictable | | Example | `number[]` | `[string, number]` | | Use case | List of items | Fixed structure like key-value pair |
🧰 Real-World Example: Returning Multiple Values
Without tuples:
function getUser() { return { name: "Pavan", age: 28 }; }
With tuples:
function getUserTuple(): [string, number] { return ["Pavan", 28]; } const [name, age] = getUserTuple(); console.log(`${name} is ${age} years old.`);
Tuples are compact, fast, and perfect for multi-value returns (like useState in React).
⚠️ Common Pitfalls
1. Forgetting order matters
let item: [number, string] = [42, "ID"]; item = ["ID", 42]; // ❌ Wrong order
2. Overusing any[]
let arr: any[] = [1, "two", true]; // Works, but loses all type safety
3. Mutating tuples (advanced)
Tuples are technically arrays, so JS mutation methods still exist - but avoid altering structure after creation.
✨ TL;DR
| Concept | Example | Description | | ------------------ | ----------------------- | ---------------------------- | | **Array** | `number[]` | List of same-type elements | | **Readonly** | `readonly string[]` | Immutable array | | **Tuple** | `[string, number]` | Fixed structure, mixed types | | **Optional Tuple** | `[string, number?]` | Optional value | | **Rest Tuple** | `[number, ...string[]]` | Variable trailing elements |
